title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Fix a commutative ring k. On the previous page Grothendieck worked with an abstract k-additive category C and a cochain complex C^0 -> C^1 -> ... in it, subject to two conditions. (a) Hom(C^i, C^j) is 0 unless j = i or j = i+1. It is k with basis id when j = i, and k with basis d^i when j = i+1. (b) Every object is a finite direct sum of C^i's. He realised this concretely by bounded acyclic chain complexes of finite free k-modules with free cycles. There C^i is K(i), the complex k --id--> k in degrees i+1 and i.

This page gives a simplicial model of the same category. C is now the category of k-linear half-simplicial (semi-simplicial) modules L_* that are 'flasque' (pi_i(L_*) = 0 for i > 0) and '∂-parfaits'. These are characterised by two equivalent conditions:
- (a) L_* is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of the basic objects C^i_* = \hat\Delta^i ⊗_Z k;
- (b) the L_n are free of finite type of constant rank on Spec k, n -> rk L_n is polynomial for n large, and L_* is flasque.
A margin note seems to add the standing hypothesis that finitely generated projective k-modules are free (e.g. k principal or local). Grothendieck needs this for the claim that C is karoubian.

A is the full subcategory on the C^i_*. It is k-linear but not stable under finite sums. The Hom table is again 0 / k·id / k·d_i, with d_i written 'T_*1'. So C^•_* = (C^i_*, T_*1) is a cochain complex in A, in C, or in k-linear half-simplicial modules: the 'universal cochain complex'.

Prop 1. For any k-additive category B, restriction gives an equivalence Hom(C,B) ≃ Hom_{k-lin}(A,B). Evaluating at the universal complex, F ↦ F(C^•_*), gives a further equivalence with B^•, the category of cochain complexes in B. In modern terms:
- A is the k-linear 'walking cochain complex': the free k-linear category on the quiver 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> ... modulo d∘d = 0.
- C ≃ Mat(A) is its additive envelope (also karoubian, under the freeness hypothesis).
- So additive functors out of C are the same thing as cochain complexes.

Example 1 (B = Ab_k). The co-Yoneda embedding C^op -> Hom_{k-lin}(C, Ab_k) ≃ Hom(A, Ab_k) ≃ Ab_k^• sends L_* to the cochain complex Hom_C(L_*, C^•_*). The next page computes this on generators (C^i_* goes to k -id-> k in degrees i, i+1). It identifies the essential image as cochain complexes of finite free modules with zero cohomology (with free cycles), i.e. split-exact bounded complexes. Example 2 does the same with Hom(-, L_*) and B = Ab_k^op.

Purpose. The aim is a Dold–Kan-type dictionary: 'perfect contractible' half-simplicial modules on one side, bounded split-acyclic complexes of free modules on the other. The construction is presumably the base for the 'dévissage' of ∂-perfect half-simplicial complexes and the study of multiplicative structures (ranks, determinant-type invariants) in the rest of the manuscript.
errors: The Hom table 0 / k / k (only j = i, i+1) does not hold for the naive representable semi-simplicial modules k[Δ^i]. There Hom(k[Δ^i], k[Δ^j]) = k^{binom(j+1,i+1)}. So \hat\Delta^i must denote a special object, something like a relative or cone object of the form k[Δ^{i+1}]/k[horn] whose normalized chains are k -> k in degrees i+1, i. The page does not define it.

Condition (b) allows ranks that are merely polynomial for n large. Under (a), with finite generators as in the previous page's model, ranks vanish for large n. So (a) ⇔ (b) needs either 'rank 0 for n large' or a different reading of \hat\Delta^i. As stated, the equivalence is unclear.

'C karoubien' and the essential-image description require that finitely generated projective k-modules be free. The margin note seems to add exactly this restriction. Without it an idempotent could cut out K(i)⊗P with P projective non-free, and C would not be karoubian.

Prop 1 asserts equivalences of functor categories, not isomorphisms; the notation '≈' is consistent with that. Hom(C,B) should be read as additive (equivalently k-linear) functors; the crossed-out subscript shows Grothendieck hesitated on this.
The equivalence Hom(C,B) ≃ Hom(A,B) only needs C = additive envelope of A, which is condition (a). B need not be karoubian. This is correct as written.

ideas.what: k-linear category A generated by C^i with Hom(C^i,C^j) = k only for j = i, i+1, and d∘d = 0 forced; k-linear functors A -> B are exactly cochain complexes in B
ideas.modern_name: walking (universal) cochain complex; chain complexes as additive functors out of the free k-linear category on N with d^2 = 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; made explicit in modern categorical Dold–Kan treatments (e.g. Lurie, Higher Algebra §1.2.3–1.2.4; Lack–Street, Combinatorial categorical equivalences of Dold–Kan type, 2015)

ideas.what: Universal property: the additive (Karoubi) envelope C of A satisfies Hom_add(C,B) ≃ Hom_lin(A,B) ≃ B^• (cochain complexes in B)
ideas.modern_name: additive envelope / Cauchy completion universal property; 'universal complex' representing the functor B ↦ Ch(B)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard enriched category theory (Street, Kelly); Dold–Kan via idempotent completion (Lack–Street)

ideas.what: Realising the universal complex inside half-simplicial (semi-simplicial) k-modules that are flasque (pi_i = 0, i > 0) and '∂-perfect', with a rank-polynomiality condition
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan-type correspondence for semi-simplicial modules restricted to finite-free contractible objects
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Kan (simplicial case, 1958); semi-simplicial variants are scattered in the literature

ideas.what: Fully faithful co-Yoneda embedding C^op -> Ab_k^•, L ↦ Hom(L, C^•_*), with essential image = bounded split-acyclic complexes of finite free modules
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda / Morita-type description of the envelope; contractible perfect complexes

missed.claim: Around 1975 Grothendieck frames a Dold–Kan-type statement as a universal property. A category of nice half-simplicial modules is the additive envelope of the 'walking cochain complex', so additive functors out of it are the same as cochain complexes in any k-additive target. This 'Dold–Kan as idempotent/additive completion' viewpoint was later made explicit by Lack–Street (2015) and in Lurie's Higher Algebra. The semi-simplicial (no degeneracies) setting with 'flasque' and '∂-parfait' objects is unusual.
missed.quote: C^•_* = (C^i_*, T_*1) est un complexe de cochaînes dans A ou dans C ou dans \hat Δ_{k-lin} - il joue le rôle du complexe de cochaînes universel.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early instance of the representing-object view of Dold–Kan, applied to semi-simplicial modules. Semi-simplicial Dold–Kan-type statements are less standard, so the setup could be of minor historical interest. The rank-polynomiality condition hints at intended Euler-characteristic or determinant applications, but these are not on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a clean but essentially formal statement: the additive envelope of the walking cochain complex has cochain complexes as its functor category. It is now folklore and explicit in Lack–Street and Lurie. The semi-simplicial framing and the 'universal cochain complex' language are a nice early touch, but not a hidden result.
transcription_corrections: 'C^i_* = \hat\Delta^i ⊗_Z k (i≥0)': the image shows 'C^i_* = \hat\Delta^{i}_{\mathbb Z} k (i≥0)' written above a crossed-out second formula with '(i≥1)'. The notation \hat\Delta is not defined on the page.
Margin note probably reads 'On suppose les modules proj. de type fini libres, par ex. k principal' (hypothesis that f.g. projectives are free).
In Example 1 the middle functor category looks like 'Hom_{a.c.}(A, Ab_k)' or 'Hom_{k-lin}(A, Ab_k)' rather than 'Hom_add'. The final target is Ab_k^• (cochain complexes), marked with a star.
'Ar. ∂-parfaits' is uncertain; it may be an abbreviation such as 'abs.' (absolument) ∂-parfaits.
